title: Supervised learning in depth
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Build the main supervised learning methods from scratch and learn when each works: linear regression by the normal equations and gradient descent, ridge and lasso regularization, logistic and softmax regression, support vector machines and the kernel trick, decision trees, bagging and random forests, gradient boosting, probability calibration, evaluation on imbalanced data, and model selection with cross-validation and hyperparameter search.
primary_reading: The Elements of Statistical Learning by Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman (free PDF)

weeks.1: Linear regression in depth: normal equations, gradient descent and diagnostics
weeks.5: Support vector machines and the margin
weeks.7: Decision trees: splitting criteria and pruning
weeks.11: Evaluation on imbalanced data: precision, recall, ROC and PR curves
weeks.12: Model selection: cross-validation and hyperparameter search

blocks.deliverable: Fit ridge regression for a range of penalties and tabulate the coefficient paths.
Train logistic regression from scratch and check its gradient.
Compute kernel matrices and classify points with a kernel method.
Week 7 midterm; grow a small decision tree by hand and in code.
Boost decision stumps and measure calibration.
Choose a model by cross-validation and report its test performance.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Model comparison study: implement logistic regression, a decision tree, a random forest and gradient-boosted stumps from scratch in plain Python, compare them on a supplied tabular classification data set with cross-validation, report accuracy, precision, recall, ROC AUC and calibration, and explain which model you would deploy and why.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
